key_insight: Social-HUMINT measures social-media exposure through what LLMs can extract and infer about users, then tests whether those profiles predict personalized engagement preferences.
engineering_relevance: Security teams can use the framework to assess public-data exposure and support analysts evaluating opportunities for personalized social engineering.
method: Unify SOCMINT and Cyber-HUMINT into 38 capabilities across the Cyber Threat Intelligence lifecycle.
Implement extraction, inference, and susceptibility assessment with an LLM-augmented multi-agent pipeline.
Compare predicted rankings of personalized engagement options with participants’ actual choices.
evidence_signal: On real participants’ public data, extraction achieved F1 = 97.3%, inferred attributes scored 4.73/5, and engagement rankings matched choices significantly above chance; experts validated the taxonomy with Fleiss’ κ = 0.92.
watch_item: Engagement-preference prediction is an indirect susceptibility measure, not evidence of successful attacks; the abstract does not report participant count.
paper_title: Social-HUMINT: An LLM-Augmented Unified Framework for Measuring Social Media Exposure
